newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police disappointed in mine clue search.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police disappointed in mine clue search.

text.p: Belgian police, hopeful of a breakthough on their 14th day searching a disused coal-mine complex for clues in a child sex and murder scandal, faced disappointment on Sunday.
The team, battling bitter cold and snow, broke through a suspicious bricked-over entrance to find it revealed only earth, Gendarmerie spokesman Guy Soumoy told reporters.

The police, visibly disappointed, had hoped the entrance, discovered on Saturday, would lead to a hideaway used by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux to hold children kidnapped for a paedophile network.
The mine search started on December 13, days after Dutroux's second wife Michele Martin indicated there was something to be found there.
"The wall did not hide anything," Soumoy told reporters, saying one door seemed to be closing after another in the search of the vast four-hectare complex.
"We have to find the right entrance to the right shaft," he said. "We are going forward slowly, but we are advancing."
Sunday's disappointment meant the search was likely to continue for several more days, despite worsening weather conditions.

The search will continue on Monday, before being interrupted for two days for the New Year, and police hope that it will be aided by a special map on a scale of one to a thousand being prepared by architects and geologists in the team.
"The snow does not disturb us more than the cold," Soumoy told reporters.
Dutroux and several alleged accomplices have been detained since August since two young girls were rescued alive from a secret dungeon at a house he owned.
The bodies of four other girls were later found buried at properties connected to Dutroux and an acquaintance, Bernard Weinstein, whose body was also discovered.
The police suspect Dutroux used part of the old tunnels linked through the 24-metre (79 feet) deep shaft to hold kidnapped children. He once lived in a caravan near the complex.
Police are now searching for at least seven missing children.
